questions.q: Which of the following is a private IP address commonly used by home routers?
questions.solution: 192.168.0.0/16 is reserved for private networks - the default address of most home routers. 172.32 lies outside the private 172.16-172.31 block, 169.254.x.x is APIPA/link-local, and 8.8.8.8 is Google's public DNS.
questions.shortcut: The private trio: 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x. Everything else is public.

questions.q: **MS-DOS**, where you typed commands like DIR and COPY on a black screen, used which type of interface?
questions.solution: DOS used a **command-line interface** — you typed commands; no windows, icons or mouse pointer. Windows brought the GUI style.

questions.q: Shift+F5 in MS PowerPoint:
options: Starts the show from the currently selected slide
questions.solution: Shift+F5 runs the presentation from the slide you are currently editing - handy while testing a single slide. F5 alone always starts from the first slide.

questions.q: Which protocol downloads incoming mail to a single device, usually removing it from the server?
questions.solution: **POP3 = Post Office Protocol** — pick up the mail like a letter-box: one download, one device.
questions.shortcut: POP Picks it off the server.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is not capable ___ handling so much pressure at work.
questions.solution: The fixed collocation is **capable of** + V-ing. *capable for / in / to* are not standard.

questions.q:
Select the word which is nearest in meaning to the given word.

VIGILANT
questions.solution: *Vigilant* = carefully watchful for danger → **alert**. 'Careless' and 'drowsy' are opposite-directed; 'hostile' shifts to temperament.

questions.q: Select the word which is most opposite in meaning to the given word.  VICTORIOUS
questions.solution: Command word = opposite. Strike the synonym decoys (triumphant, winning, successful) → **defeated**.

questions.q: Select the word which is nearest in meaning to the given word.  CHRONOLOGICAL
questions.solution: chron = time → **arranged in time order** (a chronology of events).

questions.q: Dengue fever is transmitted by which mosquito?
questions.solution: **Dengue** (a viral disease) is spread by the day-biting **Aedes** mosquito (*Aedes aegypti*), which also spreads chikungunya, Zika and yellow fever. Anopheles spreads malaria and Culex spreads filariasis.

questions.q: The RBI's single, integrated scheme for resolving customer complaints against banks and other regulated entities was introduced in:
questions.solution: The **RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021** merged the old Banking Ombudsman Scheme (1995) and other schemes into one cost-free complaint route through the RBI's central portal.

questions.q: **Gond** tribal painting is associated with —
questions.solution: **Gond** painting — the dot-and-line tribal art of the Gond community of central India (MP).

questions.q: Digboi, the site of India's oldest oil refinery, is located in which state?
questions.solution: The **Digboi** refinery in **Assam** began operating in **1901** and is the oldest operating refinery in India. Gujarat has Ankleshwar and Koyali; Mumbai High is an offshore field off Maharashtra.

questions.q: 12 men can complete a piece of work in 15 days. In how many days will 20 men complete the same work?
questions.solution: $12 \times 15 = 20 \times D$ ⇒ $D = 9$ days.

questions.q: The minimum value of $\sin\theta+\cos\theta$ for $0^\circ\le\theta\le90^\circ$ is:
questions.solution: $\sin\theta+\cos\theta$ ranges from 1 (at $\theta=0^\circ$ or $90^\circ$) to $\sqrt2$ (at $45^\circ$). The minimum is 1.
questions.shortcut: Range $[1,\sqrt2]$: min 1, max $\sqrt2$. Trap: $\sqrt2$ is the **maximum**.

questions.q: The maximum value of $\sin\theta\cos\theta$ ($\theta$ acute) is:
questions.solution: $\sin\theta\cos\theta = \frac{\sin 2\theta}{2} \le \frac12$, at $\theta = 45^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: $\frac12$ at $45^\circ$. Trap: $1$ — that is the max of $2\sin\theta\cos\theta$, not of the product.

questions.q: Ravi spends $\frac{1}{3}$ of his salary on rent and $\frac{1}{4}$ of the remaining on food. He saves the rest, which is ₹9,000. What is his salary?
questions.solution:
After rent, $\frac{2}{3}$ is left. Food $= \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{6}$ of the salary.
Savings $= 1 - \frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$ of the salary $= ₹9,000$.
Salary $= ₹18,000$.
questions.shortcut: Trap ₹21,600: taking $\frac{1}{4}$ of the whole salary gives savings $\frac{5}{12}$.

questions.q: In a survey, **70% of people watch cricket, 60% watch football and 40% watch both.** What percentage watch **neither**?
questions.shortcut: Percentages behave exactly like counts — total is 100.

questions.q: How many rectangles (squares included) are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 82 58" width="82" height="58" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="5" x2="5" y2="53"/><line x1="29" y1="29" x2="29" y2="53"/><line x1="53" y1="5" x2="53" y2="53"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="77" y2="53"/><line x1="5" y1="5" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="5" y1="29" x2="77" y2="29"/><line x1="5" y1="53" x2="77" y2="53"/></svg>
questions.solution: A full 3 × 2 grid would have 18 rectangles, but one small line in the top row is missing. Every rectangle that needs that piece as a side is lost. Counting what is left by size — 1 × 1: 4, 1 × 2: 4, 1 × 3: 2, 2 × 2: 1, 2 × 3: 1. Total = **12**.
questions.shortcut: Full-grid formula minus the rectangles that need the missing side.

questions.q: How many letters of the word **BACKGROUND** look exactly the same in a water image (considered one by one)?
questions.solution: Top-bottom symmetric capitals: B C D E H I K O X. Letter by letter in B A C K G R O U N D: B ✓, A ✗, C ✓, K ✓, G ✗, R ✗, O ✓, U ✗, N ✗, D ✓ → **5**.

questions.q:
**Statements:** Only a few keys are brass. All brass items are metal. No metal is plastic.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some keys are not plastic.
II. All keys being plastic is a possibility.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
questions.solution: The key-that-is-brass is metal, hence never plastic — that key is 'a key not a plastic' → I follows. The same key blocks all keys inside plastic → II is impossible. **Only I.**
questions.shortcut: Trace the only-a-few member through the All into the No — one journey settles both.
